Subject: RFP Q: circuit-breaker behavior & egress controls (RFP §4.3)

Marcus / Priyom —

Thanks for the RFP submission. We have a couple of clarifying questions on section 4.3 (tenant isolation & egress controls) before we proceed to the security evidence packet:

1) Circuit-breaker semantics: when runtime load exceeds thresholds, does Redwood reject at the L7 load-balancer, drop requests in the sidecar, or enqueue and degrade to a lighter model variant? Please describe the trigger metrics (latency, queue depth, token backlog) and whether the fallback is deterministic per-tenant.

2) Egress hardening: in your Private/VPC deployment, can you confirm if sidecars are allowed direct NAT/Internet access or if all outbound traffic is funneled through customer-controlled NAT gateways / egress proxies? Do you support static egress IPs for allowlisting?

3) Attack containment: if a tenant’s model is compromised (prompt injection / data exfil attempt), what automatic containment mechanisms do you execute (rate limit, blocklist, network isolation) and what is the escalation path? Timelines for detection and quarantine would be helpful.

We would like a topology diagram and a short playbook showing the circuit-breaker decision tree. Can you attach artifacts?

Regards,
Alice Tucker
Acuity Bank — InfoSec

Attachments requested: topology diagram + playbook

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vanessa from Security for the technical playbook and the attack-containment details.

High-level answers to get you unblocked:
- Circuit-breaker: deterministic per-tenant policy. We evaluate a small set of signals (per-request latency p95, request queue depth, KV-cache miss-rate). When thresholds are crossed we follow a configured policy: reject (HTTP 503), fallback to a smaller model (quantized/shorter-context variant), or redirect to a canary pool with degraded QoS. The decision tree and thresholds are configurable per-deal.
- Egress: in Redwood Private we do not require sidecar-originated direct Internet access. Outbound traffic can be routed through customer-managed NATs/proxies. Static egress IPs are available as an option for marketplace and dedicated VPCs.
- Containment: automated rate-limits + immediate tenant isolation on high-confidence exfil signals; we also perform token-level sampling and retain full audit traces for the window of the incident.

Attaching an initial topology diagram and a short playbook — Vanessa will expand with threat scenarios and detection windows.

Thanks,

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions. I’ve summarized our isolation model, the circuit-breaker decision logic, and containment responses below. I’ve attached a more formal playbook (tenant_circuit_breaker_playbook_v1.pdf).

Summary: Redwood’s multi-layer containment model
- Per-tenant runtime isolation: each tenant is pinned to an execution namespace with dedicated sidecar proxies and per-tenant token buckets. Namespaces enforce CPU/GPU soft quotas, per-tenant queue depth caps, and KV cache partitions.
- Circuit-breaker triggers (examples):
  • p95 response latency > configured SLO (default 1.5s) for > 30s
  • request queue depth > 8x baseline for a sustained 20s
  • KV-cache miss-rate delta > 40% compared to rolling baseline
  • explicit anomaly scores from our ML-based request profiler (rate of unusual instructions/payloads)
- Fallback hierarchy (applies in order; configurable per-customer):
  1) Transparent reject (HTTP 503) to upstream caller — preserves safety, fastest remediation.
  2) Failover to quantized or short-context model variant (reduced output fidelity, lower compute).
  3) Route to a canary pool with strict rate limits and enhanced monitoring (used for triage).
  4) As last resort, quarantine tenant network egress to a restricted subnet and drop outbound connections except to allowed control-plane endpoints.

Egress / network controls:
- Private (VPC) deployment options:
  • Customer-managed NAT/egress gateways: recommended for regulated environments. Sidecars are configured not to perform direct public egress; all outbound egress can be forced through customer gateways.
  • Static egress IPs: supported for dedicated pools; we publish ranges for allowlisting.
  • Egress proxy integration: supports enterprise proxies with mutual TLS.
- Hosted offering: egress is controlled by Redwood with published IP ranges and VPC NAT options for Dedicated customers.

Containment and detection timelines:
- Detection: telemetry (request-level logs, KV cache metrics, anomaly profiler) surface high-confidence exfil indicators within 0–3 minutes for severe anomalies and 10–30 minutes for lower confidence signals.
- Automated containment: when a high-confidence rule fires, the system can perform an immediate circuit-breaker action (reject or quarantine) within <5s.
- Human escalation: high-severity incidents generate a PagerDuty incident and a forensics ticket; SLA for initial human response is 30 minutes under our enterprise support tier.

Forensics & audit evidence:
- Token-level audit trails (redacted where required) retained per contractual policy. We stream logs to customer destinations (S3/GCS) or provide them via secure share links.
- Flow & DNS logs available for the egress window.
- Integration hooks: KMS/HSM-backed signing for ephemeral workspace tokens; signed kernel hashes for model bundles.

Threat scenarios and mitigations (short):
- Prompt-injection leading to exfil: mitigate via strict output filters at sidecar, anomaly profiler, and quarantine fallback.
- Lateral movement via shared KV cache: KV cache is partitioned and access-scoped; cross-tenant reads are blocked at runtime with a zero-trust enforcement layer.
- Malicious model variant introduced upstream: runtime verifies model bundle signatures before deployment; if a bundle fails verification it never reaches runtime pools.

Operational controls we recommend in contract:
- Configurable circuit-breaker policy as part of the deployment profile (default conservative thresholds for regulated orgs).
- Audit log forwarding to customer-managed buckets with retention options.
- Weekly sampling reports and an on-demand evidence pack for compliance reviews.

Attached: tenant_circuit_breaker_playbook_v1.pdf — includes decision trees, example thresholds, and sample logs for a quarantine event.

If useful, we can provide a runbook with exact threshold values for your traffic patterns and a short lab to exercise the fallback modes.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Security Architect | Redwood Inference
